title: What Moved India's Prices in September: Onion, Food and the New CPI
sourceShort: MoSPI · Consumer Price Index (base 2024) · September 2026, provisional
source: Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (National Statistics Office): Consumer Price Index (base 2024=100), press release for September 2026, PIB PRID 2322244, 12 Oct 2026, Annexures I to IV; first release of the new series, PRID 2227012, 12 Feb 2026; every all-India item, and food and onion by state, from MoSPI's eSankhyiki portal, read 14 and 15 Oct 2026. Reserve Bank of India: Resolution of the Monetary Policy Committee and Governor's Statement, 7 Oct 2026. chapters.title: Beyond food: jewellery, travel and fuel
chapters.label: 05  Beyond food: jewellery, travel and fuel

vo.text: In September, onion cost one hundred and eight percent more than a year before: more than double.
Prices across India were up five point five four percent on a year earlier, the highest this year.
Over the year, prices rose the most in one place: Puducherry.
These are September's provisional figures, from the official tables.

vo.text: Every month, MoSPI, the statistics ministry, publishes the Consumer Price Index.
Imagine a basket that cost one hundred rupees at twenty twenty-four prices.
In September, that basket would cost one hundred and nine point four nine rupees. That number is the index.
Inflation looks at one year only: this September against last September.

scenes.source: MoSPI · all-India CPI, base 2024 · PIB releases and eSankhyiki portal · Sep 2026 provisional
scenes.title: Inflation, year on year, all India
scenes.caption: 2.74% in January, then up every month. August: 4.83%. September is provisional.

vo.text: In January, inflation was two point seven four percent, and it went up every month after that.
August came in at four point eight three percent.
September: five point five four percent. That figure is provisional, and can be revised next month.
Yearly rates in the new series start in January, so there are only nine so far.

scenes.title: The new basket

vo.text: Chapter two: the new basket.

scenes.source: MoSPI · CPI base 2024: items, markets and base · PIB releases of 12 Oct 2026 and 12 Feb 2026
scenes.title: Behind the number

vo.text: The new index prices three hundred and fifty-eight items, up from two hundred and ninety-nine in the old one.
Its prices come from one thousand four hundred and sixty-five villages and one thousand four hundred and seven urban markets,
visited in person by field staff, on a weekly roster.

scenes.source: MoSPI · first release of CPI base 2024, 12 Feb 2026: division-wise weights as per the new (2024) structure
scenes.title: Food and beverages: share of the basket
scenes.caption: MoSPI regrouped the 2012 weights into the 2024 divisions so the two can be compared.

a.label: Old weights, regrouped
a.sub: Base 2012, counted in the new divisions

vo.text: The weights follow a national survey of household spending.
Counting the old basket in the new divisions, food and beverages were forty-two point six percent.
In the new basket, they are thirty-six point eight percent.

vo.text: Here are the main divisions of the basket. A thicker bar means a bigger weight.
Food and beverages are the heaviest, thirty-six point eight percent, and rose seven point three six percent, drinks included.

scenes.caption: Food alone, without drinks. Drinks rose 0.25% in September.

vo.text: Food alone, without drinks, rose five point nine seven percent in August.
In September it rose seven point seven four percent, faster than prices overall.

scenes.caption: Vegetables, tubers and pulses: 1.6% in August, 9.2% in September.

vo.text: Inside food, sugar and sweets rose fastest, thirteen point eight percent.
Fruits and nuts rose ten point eight percent.
Vegetables and pulses jumped, from one point six percent in August to nine point two percent.
Cereals rose the least, three point nine percent.

vo.text: Sugar alone, without sweets and desserts, was up twenty-nine point eight percent in a year.
Rice rose eight point three percent. Wheat rose only one point six percent.

scenes.title: The onion story

vo.text: Chapter four: the onion.

scenes.source: MoSPI · eSankhyiki portal, CPI base 2024, onion (combined), all India · Sep 2026 provisional · read 14 Oct 2026
scenes.title: Onion, year on year, all India
scenes.caption: In January onion cost 29.3% less than a year before.

vo.text: In January, onion cost twenty-nine point three percent less than a year earlier.
By June, it cost four point seven percent more.
Then it climbed fast, through July and August.
In September, onion was one hundred and eight percent above a year before.

scenes.source: MoSPI · eSankhyiki portal, CPI base 2024, onion index (combined), all India · Sep 2026 provisional · read 14 Oct 2026
scenes.title: Onion's price index, a year apart
scenes.caption: More than double in a year.

vo.text: Here is what that means in the index.
A year earlier, onion's index stood at sixty-nine.
This September it was one hundred and forty-three: more than double.

scenes.source: MoSPI · CPI base 2024, five items from PIB Annexures I and II · Sep 2026 provisional · 12 Oct 2026
scenes.title: Five kitchen items, September, year on year
scenes.caption: Some kitchen prices were lower than a year before.

vo.text: Not everything rose. Potato was down eleven point five percent on a year before, and tomato eight point six percent.
Garlic rose fifty-four point six percent, and ginger sixty-two point nine percent.

scenes.source: Ministry of Consumer Affairs · onion buffer release · PIB, 26 Aug 2026
scenes.title: What the government said on 26 August
scenes.note: Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution, press release of 26 August 2026.

tiles.caption: a kilo: the retail price the ministry announced
lakh tonnes: estimated crop of 2025 to 2026, close to the year before
lakh tonnes bought for the buffer, of 2 planned

vo.text: By the twenty-sixth of August, the government said it had begun releasing onions from its buffer stock.
It announced retail sales at thirty-five rupees a kilo, and called supplies comfortable.
It said onion prices typically rise in the festive season.

scenes.source: RBI · Governor's Statement, 7 Oct 2026, footnote 13 · rbi.org.in
scenes.text: Onion prices increased by about 85 per cent by end-September over end-June, driven by low rabi stocks and concerns over kharif arrivals amid uneven rainfall. As a result, the increase during August-September is sharper than the usual seasonal pick-up.
scenes.by: Reserve Bank of India, Governor's Statement

vo.text: Six weeks later, the RBI gave its reading.
It pointed to low rabi stocks and worries over kharif arrivals, amid uneven rain.
And it called the rise sharper than the usual seasonal pick-up.
Its figure compares end-June with end-September, and came before the September index.

vo.text: Silver jewellery cost eighty-seven point eight percent more than a year before.
Gold, diamond and platinum jewellery cost thirty point nine percent more.
In August, silver had been up even more, one hundred and six point eight percent.

scenes.title: Travel and fuel, September, year on year
scenes.caption: Prices of items in the index, all India.

vo.text: Domestic air fares rose twenty-nine point nine percent.
Diesel rose eight point four percent, and petrol seven point five percent.
Cooking gas, in cylinders and pipes, rose five point three percent.
Electricity charges fell one percent.

scenes.source: MoSPI · CPI base 2024, class and division · Sep 2026 provisional · eSankhyiki portal and PIB release of 12 Oct 2026
scenes.title: Where jewellery sits in the basket
scenes.note: Year on year, September 2026, provisional. The division: personal care, social protection and miscellaneous goods and services.

tiles.caption: its whole division, the fastest of the divisions
that division's share of the basket

vo.text: Jewellery sits in the division of personal care, social protection and miscellaneous goods and services.
That division rose thirteen point seven five percent, the fastest of all, yet it is five percent of the basket.

scenes.title: Villages and cities

vo.text: Chapter six: villages and cities.

scenes.source: MoSPI · all-India CPI, base 2024, rural, urban, combined · PIB releases · Sep 2026 provisional
scenes.title: Inflation, rural and urban
scenes.caption: In January the two were almost level: 2.73% rural and 2.75% urban.

vo.text: In January, prices in villages and cities rose at almost the same pace.
By September, villages were ahead.
Rural inflation was six point zero eight percent. Urban, four point eight eight percent.

scenes.source: MoSPI · Consumer Food Price Index and division weights, rural and urban · PIB · Sep 2026 provisional
scenes.title: Food prices, villages and cities
scenes.caption: Food and beverages are 42% of the rural basket and 30% of the urban one.

vo.text: Food rose eight point zero six percent in villages and seven point one eight percent in cities.
Food and drinks weigh more in village baskets: forty-two percent, against thirty percent in cities.
MoSPI does not say whether the two are linked, and neither do we.

scenes.note: Biggest jump from August's first figures: Jharkhand, +1.9 points. Only Assam fell.

vo.text: Here is every state and union territory.
Puducherry was highest, at six point eight six percent.
Then Tamil Nadu, six point eight one percent, and Odisha, six point seven percent.
Mizoram was lowest, at two point eight five percent.
Of the thirty-six states and territories, eleven were above the national figure.
Against August's first figures, the biggest jump was in Jharkhand, one point nine percentage points.

scenes.title: What the RBI did

vo.text: Chapter eight: what the RBI did.

scenes.source: RBI · Monetary Policy Committee: resolution of 7 Oct 2026 and minutes of the August meeting · rbi.org.in
scenes.title: The RBI's repo rate
scenes.caption: Up a quarter point (25 basis points), five days before September's prices were published.

vo.text: The repo rate is the rate at which the RBI lends money to banks for short periods.
On the seventh of October, the RBI raised it by a quarter point, to five point five percent.
Its committee voted for the rise unanimously.
That was five days before September's price figures came out.

scenes.source: RBI · Resolution of the Monetary Policy Committee, 5 to 7 Oct 2026, paragraphs 9, 17 and 18 · rbi.org.in
scenes.title: The RBI's own projections, made on 7 October
scenes.note: Minutes of the meeting: 21 October. The next meeting ends 4 December.

tiles.caption: consumer price inflation projected for the year to March 2027

vo.text: The RBI projects inflation of five point two percent for the year ending March twenty twenty-seven,
and six percent for October to December. These are the RBI's projections, not ours.
